parts:
Hey everyone! 

I am failry new to MIRT modeling and I am not quite sure the output (printed below) I have is consistent, because 4 items have negative slope values. 
The data is from 39k students in a 45 items test (4 options with 1 being correct). 

Is it normal to have this many negative slopes for a1 in such a scenario? Does that mean that for this item  people with low theta are more likely to get it right?

I also have a bunch of fairly flat curves which is making me more skeptical of wheter i did things correctly. 

One more thing I am struggling a bit to understand is how to  evaluate the impact of an item on fscores(). I want to know if there are certain items which students should focus on to get better grades. Is a1 the parameter I should watch for? Especially a1 for questions with a low d parameter?

Thank you very much for all the work put onto this, I already learned a lot from the articles and documentation and am very glad to have found this forum.

Any ideas also why  would it be that with itemtype = '3PL' the results are inconsistent?
Im also still wondering about interpreting a1 slope being negative or >6 and on how to  evaluate the impact of an item on fscores() (as explained in more detailed on thefirst post). So help on any of those matters would be greatly appreciated!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Negative a1 values and evaluating impact of item on fscores()
parts:
The large negative slopes from the 3PLM likely indicates poor convergence, as these models are notoriously difficult to estimate well without providing some type of prior parameter distributions (your output even indicates the model failed to converge). Regarding your question about which items students should focus on to obtain better grades, that depends entirely on their unobserved ability. More abled students should attempt harder questions, while less abled students should ignore hard questions and focus on the easier ones (which to them would be perceived as more difficult). 

Phil
